div.head: Ps Cn for 27.1
div.ab: Sunt et alia quamplurima animalia, que, quanquam infra septa foreste uiuunt et oneri et cure mediocrium subiacent, foreste tamen nequaquam censeri possunt, qualia sunt equi, bubali, uacce et similia.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 625 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page); Liebermann’s print has ‘curo’ (for ‘cure’, i.e. curae); transcribed as printed
div.ab: There are also very many other animals which, although they live within the enclosures of the forest and are subject to the charge and care of the middling men, can nevertheless by no means be reckoned [beasts] of the forest, such as horses, buffaloes, cows and the like.

note.seg: Gestüte im Forst kennen die Pipe rolls seit 1155; vgl. deren Indices: Eque in foresta. Verf. meint equae indomitae = siluestres (nicht eine Rasse wilder Pferde); sie stehen in Angelsächs. Urkunden und dem Domesday: Earle Landchar. 222; Napier and Stevenson Crawford char. 130; Eyton Domesday stud. I 45. Ferner hält Rievaulx im 12. Jh. neben Rindern 60 matres equas cum nutrimento suo per forestam und faldas ad equos illaqueandos; Cart. Rieval. 157. 67

The Pipe rolls know studs in the forest from 1155; cf. their indexes: Eque in foresta. The author means equae indomitae = siluestres (not a breed of wild horses); they occur in Anglo-Saxon charters and in Domesday: Earle, Landchar. 222; Napier and Stevenson, Crawford char. 130; Eyton, Domesday stud. I 45. Further, Rievaulx in the 12th century keeps, besides cattle, 60 matres equas cum nutrimento suo per forestam and faldas ad equos illaqueandos; Cart. Rieval. 157. 67

tauri silvestres in Hertfordshire in the 11th century in Mat. Paris, Gesta abb. S. Alb. I 40; cf. Harting, British animals extinct 220; and still in the 12th century near London: Will. f. Steph., Descr. London. 6. Passages of later date e.g. Mätzner s. v. bugle
Vgl. Gl Pferd 4; Büffel; Forst 16a; Davis *251. Im Ggs. zu wilden bestiae heissen domestici im 13. Jh. boves, equi, vacce in ‘Glanvill revised’ bei Maitland Coll. pap. II 286
Cf. Gl Pferd 4; Büffel; Forst 16a; Davis *251. In contrast to wild bestiae, boves, equi, vacce are called domestici in the 13th century in ‘Glanvill revised’, in Maitland Coll. pap. II 286
